history.notes: New: Touches, your own restyles of websites, from the sparkle button in the address bar. Pick an element to hide it or change its colors, font, size and corners, Zap clutter away, or write CSS; each site can have several touches, each with its own switch. Share one by link or file, or publish it to the gallery in one click: on a site, touches others published show up to try, keep and like. Shared touches can't load anything from other sites. All of them are in the Library's new Touches tab; Settings → Touches turns them off.

Color schemes get a bigger preview in Settings (Show preview): hover a scheme to try it, in light and dark. Film grain is drawn from small cached tiles, so it's smoother and stays crisp at any zoom. New Hide sidebar tools setting (Settings → Sidebar) hides Firefox's tool buttons row; the Customize sidebar button setting is gone and the button always shows.

VirusTotal check works on a private space's downloads too. Only the file's fingerprint is looked up, the result is kept in the space's encrypted data, and the report opens inside the space. Uploading the file or scanning its link says (Shares It), since those share it with VirusTotal.

A private space's downloads keep going in the background when its window closes or it locks after idle time, instead of stopping. Turn this off with Keep downloading when locked (Settings → Spaces); then they stop and Retry continues them.

Downloads in the Library: each day has its own Clear, and right-clicking a download copies its link or opens the page it came from. Failed downloads retry by themselves after network errors (Settings → Browsing). VirusTotal check (off by default) looks finished downloads up by their fingerprint and shows the result in green, yellow or red. Retry on a private space's download continues where it stopped instead of starting over.

With Expand on hover, hovering the sidebar no longer pushes the page aside after Firefox starts, and the New Tab + icon stays in place when the sidebar closes. The installers turn scripts back on in profiles where they had been turned off.
Check for updates finds a new version right after it's released, instead of up to 5 minutes later.

Restore original files (About → Your changes) puts back this version's files as shipped: edits undone, deleted files back, your copies saved first. The Mods store button moved to the Mods tab. When git has nothing new to pull because version.json was edited, About says so and shows how to fix it.

Update with git works when Firefox was started from the Start menu or a shortcut (git wasn't found before). If an update can't finish, About shows why in a box you can select and copy, with the command to run yourself.

The installers list profiles by the name Firefox shows (like Zen or Original profile), not just the folder. On Windows, Run with PowerShell keeps the window open at the end so you can read the result.
A more compact About tab with the version history, and How it works and Your changes folded away. Updates are now checked each time Firefox starts; turn off Check at startup to check only by hand.

Each space, private ones included, can have its own download folder (right-click a space → Download Folder): its downloads and Save As go there, and the Library's Open downloads folder opens it. First start now also asks for the needed restart in a notification bar.
First versioned release: an About tab in the Library, with daily update checks and in-place updates that keep your edits.
